task: Build the interrupt/resume idempotence probe (H3): add an additive resume mode to run-batch.mjs, and a resume-probe.mjs that kills the driver deterministically (boundary + mid-iteration) and reconciles the ledger identity-multiset (0 dup / 0 gap) into resume-reconciliation.json.
outcome: node resume-probe.mjs spawns run-batch (small), kills it at a boundary (SIGKILL) and mid-iteration (POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT), restarts in --resume, and writes resume-reconciliation.json showing the ledger identity-multiset == protocol cross-product exactly (0 dup / 0 gap) with the casualty resolved to a stop-or-clean-rerun; a hermetic selfcheck-m3 asserts H3 evidence-complete.
facts: M2 run-batch.mjs is append-only + identity-keyed (iterationId=replay/<scale>/<index>) but has NO resume: it runs the full campaign and its strict exact-multiset guard would reject a restart into a partial ledger.
The mid-iteration crash hook already exists: POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT (fail at the append step = after workspace write, before ledger append).
The record append is one atomic JSONL line: a kill before append = no record (clean re-run on resume); a kill mid-append = a truncated trailing line resume must skip/repair.

H3 = 100% iterations terminate in exactly one ledger record after the probed kills+resume; ledger identity multiset == protocol cross-product (0 dup / 0 gap); casualty resolves to a stop or clean re-run, never a silent half-record.
Reuses lib/instrument.mjs; reads the frozen protocol.json for the cross-product.
constraints: The run-batch resume mode is ADDITIVE: the fresh-campaign (empty/no ledger) path is UNCHANGED so M2 batch-ledger.jsonl + selfcheck-m2 stay valid.
All work in mkdtemp isolation; small scale for speed.
A duplicate iterationId on resume is a bug (the strict guard rejects dups).
resume-reconciliation.json is the H3 evidence artifact.
unknowns: Whether a mid-append truncated line actually occurs under POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT (the fault throws before write vs during) — resolved by the probe run; resume must be robust either way.
